article_text:
Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet
Breeder: T-Bud of T-Fly Genetics
THC Content: 28%
CBD Content: Low to negligible
Terpene Profile: beta-caryophyllene , myrcene , limonene

Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Good to potentially heavy
Outdoor Yield: Good

2 Scoops takes the dessert theme literally without becoming a strain built around sweetness alone. Grape Sherbet and Orange Sherbet meet in a cannabis hybrid where creamy citrus, dark fruit, earthy funk, and unusually heavy resin production compete for attention. Mature flowers often have the kind of thick trichome coating that gives them an almost glazed appearance, while purple coloration can develop beneath bright orange pistils and pale resin. The fragrance, however, is what originally distinguished the cultivar: an orange-cream aroma reminiscent of old-fashioned frozen push pops followed by a distinctly dank undertone that prevents the profile from becoming sugary or one-dimensional.
The original plant was created in Central California by T-Bud of T-Fly Genetics. Elev8 Seeds later received permission from T-Fly to release the genetics in regular seed form and describes 2 Scoops as one of T-Bud’s most prized creations. Elev8 currently lists the cultivar as Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet, with a nine-week flowering period, good yield, very high potency, and exceptional trichome production. The seed release has since been retired from the company’s active catalog.
Genetics and Lineage
The parentage of 2 Scoops is straightforward: Grape Sherbet crossed with Orange Sherbet. Rather than using dramatically different cannabis families, T-Bud doubled down on complementary Sherbet expressions. Grape Sherbet supplies the darker fruit side of the combination, pushing aromas toward grape, berries, sweetness, and occasionally deeper earthy tones. Orange Sherbet supplies the bright citrus half, adding creamy orange characteristics that can resemble sherbet, orange candy, or an orange-vanilla frozen dessert.
Bringing those two profiles together produced more than a novelty flavor cross. Elev8 emphasizes that the selected 2 Scoops plant stood apart because of the combination of extreme frost and an unusually loud terpene profile. According to the breeder’s current description, T-Bud considered it his “crown jewel” after decades of working with California cannabis genetics, while T-Fly authorized Elev8 to distribute the line as regular seed. That history makes T-Fly Genetics the appropriate original breeder attribution even though Elev8 Seeds became the better-known commercial source for the seeds.
Its balanced hybrid classification also makes sense genetically. Neither side overwhelms the experience completely, and phenotypes can lean in different directions. Some emphasize citrus cream and an upbeat mental character; others bring more grape, earth, body relaxation, and density. That variation is part of what makes seed-grown examples interesting, particularly for cultivators hunting for a keeper rather than expecting every plant to duplicate one identical commercial clone.
Effects and Experience
The first portion of the 2 Scoops high tends to be socially friendly. Mood can rise quickly, conversation becomes easier, and familiar surroundings may take on a more entertaining quality. Rather than launching immediately into heavy sedation, the marijuana often begins with an enjoyable cerebral lift that can encourage talking, listening to music, watching a movie, gaming, or simply spending time with friends. Creative thinking may also become more fluid, although concentration can start to wander as the dose increases.
Physical relaxation develops underneath that brighter opening. A comfortable heaviness may spread through the limbs while mental tension gradually loses its urgency, giving this cannabis strain a balanced progression rather than a purely energetic or purely sedating experience. Appetite can become noticeably stronger as the high matures, which fits the strain’s dessert-like personality particularly well. Later in the session, larger amounts can turn the relaxed body sensation into substantial sleepiness.
Elev8 describes the potency of its seed release as “very high,” although it does not attach a standardized THC percentage to the cultivar. That distinction is important. THC concentration can vary significantly between phenotypes, cultivation environments, and harvests, so a specific laboratory number from one batch should not be treated as a universal figure for all 2 Scoops weed.
Medical Benefits
No clinical studies have evaluated 2 Scoops as an individual medical marijuana strain. Its reported combination of mood elevation, relaxation, and appetite stimulation may nevertheless interest cannabis consumers who prefer a hybrid that can ease into physical calm without beginning with immediate sedation. Temporary stress, low mood, mental fatigue, and difficulty unwinding are among the reasons someone might favor this general effect pattern.
As the body component becomes stronger, some consumers may also find the cultivar suitable for periods of physical tension, minor aches, loss of appetite, or difficulty settling down at night. Higher doses can shift the experience considerably toward rest, making the amount consumed as important as the strain itself.
Potent THC-rich marijuana is not universally calming. Excessive intake can cause anxiety, dizziness, dry mouth, impaired coordination, or an uncomfortable sense of mental heaviness. Anyone using cannabis for a medical condition should consider the laboratory analysis of the specific product and professional medical advice rather than relying only on the reputation associated with 2 Scoops.
Flavor Profile and Aroma
Orange cream is the signature aroma. Elev8 compares the strain directly with old-school orange push pops and emphasizes that the sweetness is accompanied by noticeable funk. That combination gives the flower considerably more depth than its dessert-inspired name might suggest. Freshly opened buds can release creamy citrus first, followed by grape skins, berries, damp earth, and a pungent cannabis note underneath.
Grinding the flower tends to make the contrast stronger. Brighter orange and sugary fruit become more concentrated while peppery, earthy, or sour elements emerge from the interior of the bud. On inhalation, the flavor can resemble orange sherbet or citrus cream; the exhale often becomes darker, carrying grape, berry, and funky earth.
A definitive terpene hierarchy cannot be assigned to the original line because Elev8 does not publish a standardized laboratory terpene panel. Beta-caryophyllene, myrcene, limonene, and pinene would all be chemically plausible contributors to spicy, earthy, citrus, and herbal expressions, but actual dominance should be determined from a tested batch rather than inferred from flavor alone.
Growing Information
2 Scoops was released as a photoperiod hybrid in regular seed form, meaning growers could encounter both male and female plants rather than the feminized-only format common in many contemporary releases. Elev8 currently lists approximately nine weeks of flowering and describes production simply as “good.” Older descriptions of the line sometimes portrayed it as heavier yielding, but because the breeder does not provide a standardized grams-per-square-meter number, environmental conditions should be treated as the deciding factor.
Plant vigor is one of the cultivar’s useful characteristics. Healthy specimens can create sturdy branching capable of supporting chunky flowers, while the canopy generally responds well to topping or low-stress training. Giving the plant several strong primary branches before flowering can improve light distribution and reduce the risk of a single dominant top shading lower flower sites. A screen can also be useful when growers want to spread the canopy horizontally.
Trichome production becomes especially conspicuous late in bloom. Elev8 describes the flowers as heavily coated in frost, a characteristic that also appears repeatedly when the company uses 2 Scoops as breeding stock in later crosses. Dense resinous buds require good ventilation as flowering progresses, particularly where relative humidity remains high.
Outdoor timing has not been formally specified by the breeder. As a nine-week photoperiod cultivar, it would normally finish during autumn in the Northern Hemisphere, but exact harvest dates depend on latitude and when flowering begins. Warm, dry conditions late in the season are preferable because dense flower clusters become more vulnerable to moisture problems as they reach maturity.
FAQ
What are the genetics of 2 Scoops?
2 Scoops is Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet. It was originally created by T-Bud of T-Fly Genetics in Central California, with Elev8 Seeds later receiving permission to release the cultivar in seed form.
Is 2 Scoops indica or sativa?
It is best classified as a balanced indica/sativa hybrid. Individual plants may lean slightly toward one side, but the overall experience usually combines cerebral elevation with increasingly noticeable physical relaxation.
What does 2 Scoops taste like?
Creamy orange is the defining flavor, often compared with an orange push pop or orange sherbet. Grape, berries, sweetness, earth, and pungent funk develop underneath the citrus and give the strain a considerably richer finish.
How long does 2 Scoops take to flower?
Elev8 Seeds currently lists a flowering period of approximately nine weeks for its regular-seed release. Growers should still judge maturity from trichomes and flower development rather than harvesting automatically on a particular day.
Is 2 Scoops still available from Elev8 Seeds?
The original Elev8 Seeds release is currently listed as retired and out of stock. Flower or seeds carrying the name may still exist elsewhere, but their relationship to the original T-Fly selection should be confirmed when genetic authenticity matters.
Final Thoughts on 2 Scoops
2 Scoops works because its name accurately describes only the beginning of its personality. Grape Sherbet and Orange Sherbet provide the expected dessert foundation, but the finished weed adds substantial funk, resin, and potency to the equation. Creamy citrus can dominate the first impression before darker grape and earthy notes emerge, while the experience follows a similar progression from cheerful cerebral effects into a slower, heavier body state.
Its breeding history adds another reason for the cultivar to stand out. T-Bud of T-Fly Genetics regarded the selection highly enough that it became one of the genetics associated most strongly with his work, and Elev8 subsequently used 2 Scoops as breeding material in multiple later hybrids. For growers and cannabis enthusiasts interested in California dessert genetics, 2 Scoops offers more than sweetness: exceptional frost, strong aroma, balanced effects, and a distinctive orange-cream-and-funk profile give this retired hybrid an identity that remains easy to recognize.

Some cannabis cultivars earn their reputation through novelty, while others gain recognition by combining legendary genetics into something remarkably balanced. 24K Gold belongs firmly in the second category. Developed by the renowned breeders at DNA Genetics, this hybrid unites two iconic marijuana lineages—Kosher Kush and Tangie—to produce a plant with both luxurious flavor and deeply relaxing effects.
The name reflects more than just branding. When cultivated well, the flowers often shimmer with dense trichomes that give the buds a golden sheen under proper lighting. Combined with a vibrant citrus aroma and a calm, immersive high, the cultivar offers a sensory experience that feels refined rather than overwhelming.
In modern cannabis circles, this hybrid has become a favorite among enthusiasts who appreciate terpene-forward weed varieties . Its flavor is vivid and memorable, while the effects tend to unfold gradually, delivering both mental uplift and physical ease. For many consumers, the strain captures the ideal intersection of Kush potency and citrus-rich sativa brightness.
Genetics and Lineage
Understanding the character of this hybrid begins with examining its parents. The plant is a cross between Kosher Kush and Tangie, two cultivars that occupy very different corners of the cannabis spectrum. By bringing these genetic lines together, breeders created a marijuana strain that balances heavy indica depth with lively citrus-driven energy.
Kosher Kush contributes much of the cultivar’s structural backbone. Known for its dense buds, resin-heavy flowers, and powerful relaxation effects, this legendary Kush variety has long been prized for both potency and terpene complexity. Its earthy, spicy aroma and robust growth patterns frequently appear in descendants, and those traits carry through clearly in this hybrid .
Tangie, by contrast, introduces brightness and aromatic intensity. Derived from a lineage connected to classic California citrus strains, Tangie gained fame for its unmistakable tangerine fragrance and uplifting cerebral effects. The inclusion of this parent dramatically reshapes the hybrid’s terpene profile, infusing the flowers with a vivid orange zest aroma rarely found in Kush-dominant cannabis.
When these two lineages combine, the result is a cultivar that merges citrus sweetness with deep herbal undertones. The hybrid structure allows both parental traits to coexist rather than overpower one another. As a result, the plant offers an experience that feels rich, flavorful, and well-rounded rather than leaning too heavily toward sedation or stimulation.
Effects and Experience
The experience delivered by this cannabis variety tends to evolve in distinct stages rather than striking all at once. Shortly after consumption, many users notice a gentle elevation in mood accompanied by a subtle sense of mental clarity. The citrus-heavy terpene profile may contribute to this early phase, which often feels bright and mentally refreshing.
As the high deepens, the influence of its Kush ancestry begins to take hold. Muscles gradually loosen, and a calm warmth spreads through the body. Unlike highly sedating indica varieties , the physical effects tend to develop in a smooth, enveloping way rather than dropping users abruptly into couch-lock. This balance allows the hybrid to remain functional for many consumers, especially during relaxed social settings or creative activities.
Later stages of the experience typically bring a more pronounced sense of tranquility. Thoughts slow slightly, tension dissipates, and the body settles into a comfortable equilibrium. Many cannabis enthusiasts appreciate how the cultivar maintains a gentle mental uplift while the physical relaxation intensifies, creating a harmonious state that feels both soothing and mentally present.
Medical Benefits
Within the realm of medical marijuana , hybrids that combine mental uplift with physical comfort often appeal to a wide range of patients. This particular cultivar offers a combination of properties that may help address both psychological and physical concerns.
The mood-elevating aspect of the strain may provide support for individuals managing stress or depressive symptoms. Limonene—one of the dominant terpenes present in the plant—is frequently associated with mood enhancement and emotional clarity in cannabis research. For some patients, the gentle mental lift may help reduce the weight of everyday stressors.
Physical relaxation represents another potential benefit. The presence of myrcene and caryophyllene contributes to the strain’s calming body sensation. These compounds are often linked to anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties in cannabis, which may assist those dealing with muscle tension, minor aches, or persistent discomfort.
In addition, the hybrid’s balanced effect profile makes it suitable for individuals who want symptom relief without complete sedation. Patients seeking evening relaxation that still allows conversation, reading, or light activities often find the strain particularly appealing.
Flavor Profile and Aroma
Few marijuana cultivars display terpene expression as vividly as this one. Breaking open a well-cured bud releases an immediate burst of sweet citrus fragrance that resembles freshly peeled oranges. The influence of the Tangie lineage becomes unmistakable at this stage, producing a scent that feels bright, tangy, and slightly sugary.
As the aroma continues to develop, deeper layers emerge beneath the citrus surface. Earthy herbal notes rise from the background, accompanied by subtle hints of spice and pine. These characteristics originate from the Kush genetics, providing balance and preventing the fragrance from becoming overly sweet.
The flavor follows a similarly layered progression. Inhale often begins with a sharp citrus brightness that coats the palate with notes reminiscent of orange marmalade or candied tangerine. Midway through the inhale, the sweetness blends with herbal undertones and a faint peppery warmth. The exhale frequently reveals earthy Kush notes mixed with lingering citrus zest, leaving a complex aftertaste that persists long after the smoke or vapor dissipates.
Growing Information
Cultivating this hybrid can be rewarding for growers who appreciate terpene-rich cannabis plants. The cultivar typically develops a sturdy structure with moderate vertical growth, inheriting characteristics from both parents. Branching patterns tend to be fairly strong, allowing the plant to support dense flower clusters during the later stages of flowering.
Indoor growers generally observe a flowering period of around nine to ten weeks. During this phase, buds begin to swell noticeably while producing thick layers of sticky resin. The flowers often display vibrant green tones accented by orange pistils and heavy trichome coverage, giving the buds their signature golden shimmer when exposed to light.
Outdoor cultivation performs best in warm, Mediterranean-style climates where the plant can receive abundant sunlight. Proper airflow and humidity management are important, especially late in the flowering stage when dense buds can retain moisture. When grown under optimal conditions, the cultivar can produce satisfying yields of aromatic flower packed with citrus-heavy terpene content.
FAQ
What is 24K Gold strain?
24K Gold is an indica-dominant cannabis hybrid created by crossing Kosher Kush with Tangie. The strain was bred by DNA Genetics and is also commonly referred to as Kosher Tangie.
Is 24K Gold indica or sativa?
The cultivar is generally classified as an indica-dominant hybrid. Despite that classification, it retains some uplifting mental qualities from its Tangie lineage.
What does 24K Gold weed taste like?
The flavor is strongly citrus-forward, often described as sweet orange or tangerine. Beneath the bright citrus layer, earthy Kush notes and mild spice add depth to the overall taste.
How strong is 24K Gold marijuana?
Most lab-tested samples fall between 18% and 24% THC. The effects tend to feel balanced, delivering both mental elevation and relaxing body sensations.
Is 24K Gold good for beginners?
Because the THC levels can reach the mid-20% range, beginners may want to start with small doses. Experienced cannabis users usually find the effects manageable and pleasantly balanced.
Final Thoughts on 24K Gold
Among modern cannabis hybrids, few strains combine terpene intensity and relaxing effects as successfully as 24K Gold. By pairing the citrus brilliance of Tangie with the deep, resin-rich character of Kosher Kush, breeders created a cultivar that feels both flavorful and substantial.
The plant’s appeal extends beyond its aroma and potency. Its layered effects make it adaptable to a variety of situations, from laid-back evenings with friends to quiet moments of personal relaxation. Meanwhile, growers appreciate the cultivar for its sturdy structure, resin-heavy buds, and vibrant terpene expression.
For those exploring premium marijuana varieties that showcase both Kush power and citrus elegance, this hybrid remains a standout choice. Its combination of heritage genetics, aromatic complexity, and balanced effects ensures that it continues to hold a respected place in the evolving world of cannabis cultivation and consumption.

Genetics and Lineage
The genetic blueprint behind 3 Kings reads like a who’s who of classic cannabis breeding . Its three parent strains—Headband, Sour Diesel, and OG Kush—each contributed distinct characteristics that shaped the final cultivar.
Headband itself originates from a cross between Sour Diesel and OG Kush, which means two of the plant’s parents already share a genetic relationship. Headband became famous for its distinctive pressure-like sensation around the temples and its balanced combination of euphoria and body relaxation. By crossing Headband with its foundational strains again, breeders effectively reinforced the defining characteristics of those original genetics.
Sour Diesel contributes the unmistakable sharpness that dominates the strain’s aroma and mental effects. Long celebrated for its fast-acting cerebral high, this classic sativa influence provides the energetic backbone of the hybrid. The strain’s lively headspace—often associated with creativity, focus, and motivation—can largely be traced back to the Diesel lineage.
OG Kush, on the other hand, supplies the grounding force within the genetic mix. Known for its dense buds, resin production, and earthy pine flavor, OG Kush stabilizes the hybrid and introduces the deep body relaxation that balances the cerebral uplift. The presence of OG genetics also contributes to the plant’s strong structural growth and robust terpene expression.
Together, these three parents create a cultivar that embodies the spirit of classic American marijuana breeding. Rather than introducing novelty genetics, the strain refines and intensifies the qualities that made these legendary cultivars famous in the first place.

Instead of arriving abruptly, the high tends to build in waves, beginning with a subtle lift in mood that gradually evolves into a brighter, more energized state of mind. Many cannabis consumers describe a sharpened sense of focus during the early phase, making the cultivar suitable for creative work, conversation, or outdoor activities.
As the high continues to develop, a gentle physical warmth begins to spread throughout the body. This stage reflects the influence of the OG Kush genetics, adding a comfortable relaxation without overwhelming sedation. Muscles loosen, tension eases, and the body settles into a calm but functional state. The combination of these effects often allows users to remain active while still enjoying the soothing properties of the weed.
Toward the later stages of the experience, the energetic edge tends to soften. Rather than producing heavy couch-lock, the cultivar transitions into a mellow equilibrium where the mind remains alert but the body feels pleasantly relaxed. This balanced progression makes the hybrid appealing for daytime or early evening use when users want stimulation without losing physical comfort.
Medical Benefits
Medical marijuana patients often gravitate toward cultivars that provide both mental uplift and physical relief, and this hybrid offers a combination of effects that can support several therapeutic goals. The uplifting cerebral component may help individuals dealing with stress, fatigue, or low mood. The energetic clarity associated with the strain can encourage productivity and mental engagement, which some patients find helpful when navigating depressive symptoms.
At the same time, the cultivar’s physical relaxation can assist those experiencing chronic tension or mild pain. The presence of caryophyllene and myrcene in the terpene profile contributes to its calming body sensation. These compounds are frequently associated with anti-inflammatory properties in cannabis, potentially supporting relief from muscle soreness or everyday aches.
Another area where the strain may offer value is stress management. The hybrid’s balanced nature allows the mind to remain clear while the body unwinds, creating a state that many patients describe as mentally refreshing. For individuals seeking a marijuana strain that supports daytime symptom management without excessive sedation, this cultivar often fits that role effectively.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Once the initial sharpness fades slightly, deeper aromas begin to emerge. Earthy pine and herbal undertones develop in the background, reflecting the OG Kush lineage. These notes add depth and complexity to the fragrance, preventing the profile from becoming overly acidic or one-dimensional.
The flavor closely mirrors the aromatic experience but with additional nuance. Inhale typically delivers a tangy citrus bite followed by a wave of earthy spice. As the smoke or vapor lingers on the palate, subtle pine and pepper notes become noticeable. This layered flavor progression reflects the cultivar’s terpene composition, with limonene providing citrus brightness, caryophyllene adding spice, and myrcene contributing herbal depth.
Growing Information

Growers often observe strong vertical development during the vegetative stage , which can lead to tall plants if left unmanaged. Training techniques such as topping, low-stress training, or screen-of-green methods are commonly used to control height and encourage even canopy development.
Flowering generally takes around nine to ten weeks indoors. During this period, the plant begins producing dense buds coated in a noticeable layer of resin. The flowers typically display bright green coloration with vibrant orange pistils and a heavy trichome coating that gives the buds a frosted appearance. Proper airflow becomes important in the later stages of flowering , as the dense structure of the buds can trap moisture.
Outdoor cultivation tends to thrive in warm, sunny environments with consistent airflow. When grown under favorable conditions, the plant can produce generous yields of aromatic flower. Because the terpene profile is quite pungent, growers should be aware that the scent can become extremely strong during late flowering, making odor management an important consideration for discreet operations.
FAQ
What strain is 3 Kings?
3 Kings is a sativa-dominant hybrid created by combining three well-known marijuana strains: Headband, Sour Diesel, and OG Kush. The cultivar blends the energetic effects of Diesel genetics with the relaxing qualities of Kush.
Is 3 Kings a strong cannabis strain?
Most versions of the strain test between 18% and 24% THC, placing it in the moderately strong to potent category. The effects are typically balanced rather than overwhelming, making it manageable for experienced cannabis consumers.
What does 3 Kings weed taste like?
The flavor combines sour citrus and diesel fuel with earthy pine undertones. Many users describe the taste as lemony and skunky with a peppery finish that reflects the strain’s complex terpene profile.
Is 3 Kings good for daytime use?
Because the hybrid offers mental stimulation without heavy sedation, many people prefer it for daytime or early evening consumption. The energizing qualities make it suitable for creative activities and social settings.
How long does 3 Kings take to flower?
Indoor flowering usually takes around nine to ten weeks. Outdoor plants are typically ready for harvest during the early to mid-autumn season depending on the climate.
Final Thoughts on 3 Kings
Within the world of modern cannabis, some cultivars stand out not because they introduce something entirely new but because they perfect what already works. 3 Kings fits squarely into that category. By combining three legendary marijuana strains, breeders created a hybrid that showcases the defining strengths of classic American cannabis genetics .
The cultivar’s layered high—starting with cerebral brightness before settling into relaxed equilibrium—makes it versatile across many situations. Creative projects, social gatherings, or outdoor adventures all pair well with the balanced energy this strain delivers. Meanwhile, its terpene-rich aroma ensures that the sensory experience remains just as memorable as the effects.
For growers, the plant offers strong growth, impressive resin production, and a terpene profile that fills a room with unmistakable diesel-kush intensity. For consumers, it delivers a sophisticated weed experience shaped by some of the most influential genetics in cannabis history . Few hybrids manage to combine heritage, potency, and complexity as effectively as this one.

9 Pound Hammer is one of those marijuana strains whose name becomes understandable shortly after the effects develop. Created by Jinxproof Genetics, this strongly indica-dominant hybrid was designed around the unusually fruity Gooberry cultivar, with Jesus OG Kush added to improve plant vigor, structure, and production. The resulting weed combines sweet grape and melon with lime, earthy Kush, pine, and Skunk while producing hard, resin-heavy flowers capable of turning deep purple and orange near maturity. Jinxproof describes 9 Pound Hammer as the crown jewel of the breeder’s catalog and still offers the original genetics today, listing the cultivar as 90% indica, roughly 21% or higher THC, a 50–60 day flowering period, and a heavy commercial-grade yield.
The strain became particularly well known for its progression from a brief euphoric lift into increasingly powerful body relaxation. That heavy finish helped inspire the “Hammer” name and made the cultivar an enduring favorite among consumers who prefer old-school fruit, Kush, and Skunk characteristics over the sweeter Cookies-derived profiles that dominate much of the modern market.
Genetics and Lineage
The breeder-confirmed lineage of 9 Pound Hammer is Gooberry × Jesus OG Kush. Jinxproof Genetics explains that Gooberry was selected for its exceptional fruit terpenes, resin production, and dramatic autumn coloration, but it had relatively modest production. Jesus OG Kush was brought into the project to add greater vigor, stronger structure, and substantially improved yield while preserving the aromatic qualities of the Gooberry parent.
Gooberry contributes much of the cultivar’s recognizable grape, berry, melon, and earthy character. It also helps produce the oversized calyxes and purple coloration commonly seen in desirable 9 Pound Hammer phenotypes. Jesus OG Kush adds more height and structural strength along with citrus, pine, fuel, and Kush characteristics . Jesus OG itself is associated with Hells Angel OG and Jack the Ripper ancestry, which explains why some descriptions simplify 9 Pound Hammer’s pedigree into Gooberry, Hells OG , and Jack the Ripper. The actual breeding cross performed by Jinxproof, however, is more accurately written as Gooberry × Jesus OG Kush.
The cultivar was once distributed through Subcool’s TGA Genetics network, which contributed to confusion over its breeder. Jinxproof has publicly clarified that he created 9 Pound Hammer and that Subcool distributed the strain rather than breeding it. The genetics later returned fully to Jinxproof’s own catalog, where the original version remains available.
Effects and Experience
The first stage of the high can feel brighter than the 90% indica classification suggests. A warm euphoric shift may arrive quickly, improving mood and making music, television, conversation, or a quiet evening more absorbing. There can be a brief period of mental clarity and pleasant stimulation before the strain begins showing the heavier qualities behind its name.
As the experience develops, physical relaxation becomes much more pronounced. Limbs may begin to feel heavy, muscular tension can soften, and motivation for demanding activity tends to decline. With a moderate dose, the change may feel like gradually sinking into a comfortable chair. Larger amounts can push the strain toward pronounced couch-lock and sleepiness, making 9 Pound Hammer more naturally suited to later-day use than situations requiring sustained attention.
Jinxproof currently describes the strain as a high-THC cultivar at roughly 21% or more, but modern batches can vary significantly. Consumers with limited THC tolerance should approach it conservatively because excessive amounts can produce dizziness, dry mouth, impaired coordination, anxiety, or stronger sedation than intended.
Medical Benefits
The deeply relaxing reputation of 9 Pound Hammer has made it popular among some medical marijuana consumers seeking cannabis for evening use. Its combination of initial mood elevation followed by a stronger physical phase may appeal to people who prefer a cultivar that does not become immediately sedating but eventually settles into substantial relaxation.
Some consumers may also report using heavy indica-dominant strains when dealing with temporary discomfort, tension, appetite changes, or difficulty winding down at night. These experiences are subjective, however, and they should not be interpreted as evidence that 9 Pound Hammer treats a particular medical condition. The actual effect can change considerably with THC concentration, terpene chemistry, individual sensitivity, tolerance, and dose.
There are no clinical trials establishing 9 Pound Hammer itself as a treatment for insomnia, chronic pain, anxiety, or another disorder. Anyone using cannabis medically should rely on the laboratory analysis of the specific product and appropriate healthcare guidance rather than assuming a strain name guarantees a therapeutic response.
Flavor Profile and Aroma
Fruit defines the opening aroma. Jinxproof specifically emphasizes grape, melon, and lime characteristics, with the prized Gooberry-leaning phenotype producing particularly strong fruity terpenes. Underneath that sweetness are earth, pine, Skunk, and Kush-like fuel, preventing the flower from tasting like a simple candy strain.
The terpene chemistry is not fixed from one harvest to another. A regulated 9 Pound Hammer concentrate tested by Green Analytics in New York contained 4.69% total terpenes and was led by alpha-pinene, beta-myrcene, beta-pinene, beta-caryophyllene, humulene, limonene, and alpha-bisabolol. Because that analysis was performed on a processed vape product rather than raw flower, it should be treated as an example of commercial 9 Pound Hammer terpene expression rather than a universal fingerprint for the cultivar.
In flower, the flavor usually begins with sweet grape and mixed berries before moving toward melon and tart lime. Earthy pine, pepper, and mild diesel become stronger on the exhale. Some phenotypes can lean distinctly toward grape candy, while others emphasize citrus and Kush. Proper curing helps preserve the brighter fruit notes that distinguish the cultivar from more conventional earthy indica marijuana.
Growing Information
Jinxproof bred 9 Pound Hammer to correct Gooberry’s relatively modest production, and high yield remains one of the strain’s defining horticultural traits. The breeder describes the plant as vigorous, heavy-producing, and suitable for commercial-scale cultivation. Flowering takes approximately 50–60 days, which is relatively quick for a hybrid capable of producing such dense and resinous buds.
The most desirable phenotype leans toward Gooberry, producing oversized calyxes that build into hard, compact flowers with abundant trichomes. Jinxproof notes that resin can begin appearing surprisingly early, sometimes during the later vegetative period. Plants respond well to topping, pruning, and SCROG-style canopy management, allowing growers to spread productive branches across the available light footprint.
As flowering progresses, some plants develop deep purple foliage and flowers contrasted by bright orange pistils. Dense buds require good airflow, particularly late in bloom when excess humidity can become problematic. Outdoors, the short flowering period can allow harvest around late September or early October in suitable climates, although actual maturity depends on latitude, weather, and phenotype. Rather than relying only on calendar dates, growers should use flower development and trichome maturity to judge the final harvest window.
FAQ
What are the genetics of 9 Pound Hammer?
9 Pound Hammer is Gooberry × Jesus OG Kush , bred by Jinxproof Genetics. Gooberry supplied fruit terpenes, resin, and color, while Jesus OG Kush was selected to improve vigor, plant structure, and production.
Is 9 Pound Hammer indica or sativa?
Jinxproof Genetics classifies it as approximately 90% indica and 10% sativa . Its experience reflects that background, beginning with some euphoria before progressing toward significantly stronger physical relaxation and sedation.
How strong is 9 Pound Hammer?
The breeder currently lists potency at approximately 21% THC or higher . Individual commercial flower can test above or below that level depending on the phenotype, environment, harvest timing, and laboratory methodology.
What does 9 Pound Hammer taste like?
Grape, melon, berries, and lime dominate the sweeter side of the profile. Earth, pine, Skunk, pepper, and mild diesel provide a darker Kush-like background.
How long does 9 Pound Hammer take to flower?
Jinxproof Genetics lists an indoor flowering period of approximately 50–60 days . The relatively fast finish is one of the cultivar’s most useful growing characteristics, especially when combined with its heavy yield potential.
Final Thoughts on 9 Pound Hammer
9 Pound Hammer has remained relevant because its breeding goal was practical as well as sensory. Jinxproof started with Gooberry, a cultivar valued for grape-and-melon terpenes, colorful flowers, and resin but limited by modest production. Crossing it with Jesus OG Kush strengthened the plant, raised yield potential, and introduced Kush structure without erasing the qualities that made Gooberry worth preserving. The resulting 90% indica hybrid flowers in only 50–60 days and produces dense, heavily frosted buds with enough weight for Jinxproof to describe the cultivar as commercial-grade.
Its personality is just as recognizable after harvest. Sweet grape, berries, melon, and lime sit over earth, pine, Skunk, and fuel, while the high transitions from an initially pleasant cerebral lift into the deep body relaxation behind the strain’s memorable name. In a modern cannabis market filled with dessert hybrids, 9 Pound Hammer remains a distinctly Pacific Northwest-style classic—fruit-forward without being sugary, powerful without relying on extreme THC marketing, and historically important enough that Jinxproof still identifies it as the signature cultivar of his breeding program.

Genetics and Lineage
Sherbinskis identifies Acai Berry Gelato as a member of the original Gelato family derived from Sunset Sherbert × Thin Mint Cookies. Rather than being a completely separate cross built around an acai-flavored parent, it is a selected expression from the same genetic foundation that produced several of the breeder’s best-known cultivars. This distinction is important because competing pedigrees have circulated over the years, but the breeder’s current genetic record places Acai Berry firmly within the Sunset Sherbert and Thin Mint Cookies Gelato family.
Sunset Sherbert contributes a substantial amount of fruit, color, sweetness, and physical relaxation. Its own background combines Girl Scout Cookies with Pink Panties , bringing together Cookies-family density and resin with sweet fruit, Kush influence, and colorful flower. Thin Mint Cookies adds another concentrated dose of Cookies genetics along with mint, earth, sweetness, resin, and strong cannabinoid potential. When those parents were combined, the resulting Gelato population contained enough variation for different selections to develop distinct identities despite sharing the same foundational cross.
Acai Berry Gelato emerged as one of the fruit-forward keepers. Where Bacio became closely associated with gas and floral notes and Mochi developed a doughier personality, Acai Berry emphasized berry aromas and particularly dark coloration. This makes the cultivar useful for understanding Gelato genetics as a family rather than a single uniform strain. The same cross can produce plants that diverge noticeably in aroma, growth, pigmentation, and effects when breeders identify and preserve exceptional individual phenotypes.

As the session progresses, a softer body component begins to appear. Higher servings naturally shift the experience toward greater heaviness and mental haze.

Citrus provides a brighter top note, giving the aroma enough acidity to keep the dense fruit from becoming syrupy. Some batches also carry tropical characteristics that can suggest ripe fruit beneath the berry core.
Cream appears underneath that brightness and ties the cultivar back to the Gelato family. The sweetness is smooth rather than sugary, creating a soft dessert-like foundation behind the fruit. Earth develops as the flowers are broken apart, while traces of mint, spice, or fuel may occasionally emerge depending on the specific cut and cultivation conditions. The result is richer than a simple berry strain but generally less petroleum-heavy than many modern candy-gas hybrids.
On the palate, berries and citrus commonly arrive first before creamy sweetness spreads through the middle of the inhale. Earth and mild spice linger through the finish, particularly when the flower is combusted. Vaporization can preserve more of the brighter berry and tropical notes, while smoking tends to emphasize the deeper Cookies-family base. Slow drying and a patient cure are important because the volatile fruit characteristics can disappear quickly if harvested cannabis is exposed to excessive heat or rapidly reduced humidity.

Topping, low-stress training , and a screen or trellis can redirect growth horizontally, giving multiple branches equal access to light while preventing the upper canopy from becoming dominant. Moderate pruning beneath the canopy also improves airflow and focuses production on flowering sites capable of reaching full maturity.

Continuous airflow and controlled humidity become especially important late in bloom because thick flowers can retain moisture within the canopy.
Outdoor cultivation works best where warm weather continues well into autumn. In many Northern Hemisphere environments, plants finish during October, although local photoperiod, latitude, and climate determine the actual date. Full sunlight can increase vigor substantially, but the dense flowers should be protected from extended rain as harvest approaches . The cultivar rewards growers who prioritize quality, color, resin, and terpene preservation rather than pushing the plant solely for weight.

What strains make Acai Berry Gelato?
Acai Berry Gelato is a Sherbinskis selection from the Gelato family, whose breeder-confirmed foundation is Sunset Sherbert × Thin Mint Cookies. It is not a cross involving an actual Acai-named parent; the name refers to the berry-forward character of the selected cultivar.

Acai Berry Gelato is widely circulated under the Acai Gelato and Gelato #49 names. It represents the dark, fruit-forward selection within the original Sherbinskis Gelato family.

Acai Berry Gelato demonstrates the diversity hidden inside one of modern cannabis breeding’s most famous families. It shares Sunset Sherbert × Thin Mint Cookies genetics with other Sherbinskis Gelato selections, yet phenotype selection pulled the cultivar toward a very different destination. Dark berries, tropical fruit, citrus, nearly black-purple flowers, and a brighter cerebral effect separate it from siblings built around stronger gas, dough, or physical heaviness.
The plant itself rewards growers willing to manage its stretch and accept moderate rather than enormous yields. A roughly 9–10-week bloom produces dense, heavily frosted flowers with exceptional visual appeal, while careful environmental management can preserve the berry-forward terpene profile that gives the cultivar its identity. Its deep pigmentation makes it striking in the garden, but aroma and finished quality remain more important than color alone.
For consumers, the strain provides a useful alternative to the stereotypical Gelato experience. The high can begin social, creative, and mentally energetic before settling into smooth physical relaxation, while the flavor moves through berry, citrus, cream, and earth rather than relying heavily on gas. Acai Berry Gelato ultimately stands as one of the clearest examples of how a carefully chosen phenotype can transform familiar genetics into a cannabis cultivar with a personality entirely its own.

These characteristics gradually became associated with the region’s marijuana harvests.

Royal Queen Seeds gives the direct formula as AK-47 × ruderalis. Behind the AK-47 side lies a more complicated international ancestry. Serious Seeds , breeder of the original AK-47, states that Simon developed the strain from Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan seed stock after extensive selection work in the early 1990s. Serious Seeds still keeps the precise recipe private, but confirms those four geographic sources and describes the original as a predominantly sativa hybrid.
RQS used AK-47 genetics as the foundation and introduced a high-performing ruderalis line to create automatic flowering. The resulting composition shifts to 40% indica, 35% sativa, and 25% ruderalis. That addition matters primarily in the garden: flowering begins according to plant maturity rather than requiring progressively longer nights. It also means Royal AK Auto is not genetically identical to the original Serious Seeds AK-47 or to AK-47 autoflowers sold by other breeders. A strain name is not a standardized pharmaceutical formulation.

Although 15% THC is lower than many modern cultivars exceeding 20%, unwanted reactions are still possible. NIDA notes that cannabis can produce anxiety, fear, distrust, or panic in some people, particularly after larger amounts or exposure to stronger products. The breeder-supported automatic profile remains primarily earthy, peppery, spicy, and sour.

Because this is an autoflower, severe early stress is less forgiving than it would be with photoperiod cannabis; the plant continues toward flowering regardless of whether it has fully recovered.
Outdoor cultivation works on a calendar determined by germination rather than autumn daylight. That allows growers in suitable legal climates to finish plants before traditional photoperiod marijuana reaches maturity and potentially schedule more than one crop during a long season. RQS also notes that Royal AK Auto handles a variety of environments and performs well in somewhat cooler conditions. Strong early growth, adequate sunlight or indoor lighting, careful watering, and steady airflow remain more important than complicated training methods.

The RQS version is AK-47 × ruderalis. The original AK-47 parent developed by Serious Seeds traces to Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan seed stock, although breeder Simon has never publicly revealed the exact recipe or proportions of those landrace influences.

Royal Queen Seeds currently lists THC at up to 15% with low CBD. That places it below many contemporary 20–30% THC cultivars, but it can still produce significant intoxication, particularly for consumers with low tolerance.

RQS gives a total life cycle of approximately 11–12 weeks, with its technical data listing harvest around 75–85 days after sprouting. Flowering itself generally occupies about 45–55 days.

Indoor plants can produce up to approximately 350 g/m². Outdoor specimens generally yield around 110–160 g per plant under suitable conditions. Lighting, climate, root health, nutrition, and early plant development all influence final production.

AK-47 Auto translates a historic cannabis family into a smaller, faster, and easier cultivation format without trying to compete in the modern race for maximum THC. The flavor stays rooted in earth, pepper, spice, and sourness, while the high favors laughter, motivation, and sociability over immediate couch-lock.
Its heritage adds another dimension. The AK side ultimately reaches back to Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan seed stock used by Serious Seeds to create the original AK-47 in 1992, connecting this modern automatic weed to one of the defining hybrid families of the 1990s. For growers, manageable size, straightforward training, respectable yields, and automatic flowering make it accessible without being uninteresting. For consumers, moderate potency and savory old-school flavor provide an alternative to today’s ultra-strong dessert hybrids. Keeping Royal Queen Seeds attached to the name remains important because other breeders produce different AK-47 autos, but within the RQS catalog, Royal AK Auto is a practical interpretation of a genuine cannabis classic.

For an Alien Labs-focused strain profile, Animal Mints backcross genetics are the appropriate lineage.
Animal Mints sits at the center of one of the most influential breeding families of the modern marijuana era. Seed Junky created the cultivar from Animal Cookies and SinMint Cookies , building a plant prized for dense resin, powerful potency, creamy cookie aromas, and a cooling herbal character. It later became an important parent of Wedding Cake, Kush Mints, Animal Face , and numerous other high-profile hybrids. Backcrossing toward Animal Mints intensifies those characteristics rather than radically changing them, which explains why Alien Mints often resembles an exaggerated version of the broader family: more frost, deeper gas, thicker vanilla sweetness, and an especially powerful hybrid high.
The family connection to Wedding Cake is particularly evident in the aroma. Alien Labs has described the strain’s motor-oil and vanilla funk as reminiscent of Wedding Cake taken to another level. That resemblance makes genetic sense because Wedding Cake itself belongs to the Animal Mints family. Alien Mints therefore represents less of a new genetic direction than a concentrated exploration of traits that made Seed Junky’s Mints lines important in the first place.
Effects and Experience
Alien Mints often begins with a surprisingly bright head change. The first several minutes can bring an elevated mood, increased interest in conversation, and a more immersive response to music, entertainment, food, or creative activities. Thoughts may become active without necessarily feeling scattered, and experienced consumers can sometimes remain reasonably functional during the opening portion of the high. This cerebral character is one reason the cultivar is commonly described as a balanced hybrid rather than a purely sedating indica.
Physical relaxation gradually becomes more noticeable as the experience matures. Shoulders may loosen, tension seems less prominent, and the desire to settle into a comfortable environment increases. Instead of switching suddenly from stimulation to sedation, Alien Mints usually blends the two sensations. Moderate servings may remain suitable for social evenings, movies, gaming, or casual activities, whereas larger doses can shift the balance firmly toward physical heaviness and reduced motivation.
Potency deserves respect. Animal Mints-family cannabis regularly reaches the upper 20% THC range, and strong Alien Mints flower can be particularly unforgiving when overconsumed. Excessive amounts may produce dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, impaired short-term concentration, racing thoughts, or anxiety before the relaxing phase becomes dominant. Consumers with low THC tolerance should start conservatively despite the strain’s smooth flavor and approachable hybrid character.
Medical Benefits
The progression from cerebral elevation toward physical calm may appeal to medical marijuana patients looking for cannabis that can help them unwind without beginning with immediate lethargy. Some consumers gravitate toward this type of hybrid when temporary stress, physical tension, appetite reduction, low mood, or discomfort interferes with normal relaxation. The more functional opening may be useful earlier in the evening, while the heavier second half can become increasingly appropriate as activity winds down.
Terpenes commonly associated with Animal Mints-family flower include beta-caryophyllene, limonene, myrcene, and linalool. Caryophyllene contributes dry pepper and spice, limonene adds citrus brightness, myrcene reinforces earthy and herbal qualities, and linalool can supply softer floral elements. Those aromatic compounds help shape the sensory character of the weed, but their presence does not mean Alien Mints has been clinically demonstrated to treat anxiety, insomnia, chronic pain, depression, or another medical condition.
Patients should look at the laboratory certificate for the specific batch being considered because cannabinoid and terpene concentrations can change substantially between cultivators and harvests. Anyone taking prescription medication or managing significant psychiatric, cardiovascular, or other medical conditions should discuss high-THC cannabis use with an appropriate healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma
A properly cured jar of Alien Mints tends to open with gas before sweetness. Petroleum, motor oil, and earthy funk form the heavier foundation, but creamy vanilla quickly appears above them. Breaking apart the flower can expose cookie dough, minty herbs, pine, pepper, and a subtle sweet nuttiness. Alien Labs’ own product description emphasizes gassy motor oil and vanilla funk, a combination that captures the cultivar much more accurately than the name alone.
The flavor is somewhat smoother than the aroma suggests. Vanilla and creamy dough can lead the inhale, followed by mint, pine, and mild citrus. Diesel develops more heavily through the middle of the palate before an earthy, peppery finish remains after exhalation. Some expressions lean strongly toward sweet cookies, while others bring the greasy fuel component to the foreground.
Despite the word “Mints,” the profile should not necessarily be expected to taste like peppermint candy or menthol. The mint character is usually herbal and cooling rather than confectionery. Combined with vanilla and gas, it gives the flower a distinctly modern California flavor without erasing the darker earth and fuel underneath.
Growing Information
Authentic Alien Labs Alien Mints has primarily circulated as finished flower rather than as a widely documented retail seed line, so precise breeder specifications for flowering time and yield are limited. Its Animal Mints background provides a reasonable cultivation framework. Animal Mints generally requires roughly nine to ten weeks of flowering and develops dense, trichome-heavy buds on a relatively structured hybrid plant. Growers working with verified clone material should therefore treat published timing estimates as starting points rather than guaranteed harvest dates.
Indoors, canopy management can improve production considerably. Topping during vegetation encourages additional leaders, while low-stress training allows light to reach more flowering sites. The plant’s dense flower development makes an open canopy preferable to excessive interior foliage. Removing weak lower branches before late bloom can redirect resources toward the upper flowers while creating better airflow around the plant.
Trichome production becomes one of the cultivar’s defining visual traits during flowering. The buds can appear almost silver under strong lighting as resin accumulates across the calyxes and surrounding leaves. That density makes late-bloom humidity management important. Constant circulation and reasonable humidity reduce the risk of moisture remaining trapped inside compact flowers.
Outdoor cultivation is most practical in climates with warm days, strong sunlight, and relatively dry autumn weather. An early-to-mid-October finish is a reasonable estimate in many Northern Hemisphere locations, although phenotype and latitude can move that window. Growers should use trichome development and flower maturity rather than a predetermined date to decide when to harvest. Slow drying and a patient cure are particularly worthwhile because rapid post-harvest processing can erase the vanilla and mint notes while leaving a much flatter earthy-gas profile.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Alien Mints?
The Alien Labs version of Alien Mints is Animal Mints × Animal Mints, essentially an Animal Mints backcross bred by Seed Junky Genetics. Alien Labs-associated product descriptions specifically identify the cultivar this way. Other unrelated strains have also been sold under the Alien Mints name, so breeder information is important when confirming genetics.
Who bred Alien Mints?
Seed Junky Genetics bred the Animal Mints backcross associated with Alien Mints, while Alien Labs selected, cultivated, and popularized the well-known commercial version.
Is Alien Mints indica or sativa?
Alien Mints is generally treated as a balanced or slightly indica-leaning hybrid. The experience reflects that middle ground, beginning with cerebral euphoria and social energy before gradually developing stronger body relaxation.
How strong is Alien Mints?
It is considered high-potency cannabis. Premium expressions commonly fall somewhere in the mid-to-upper 20% THC range, and Animal Mints genetics are capable of approaching or exceeding 30% in exceptional batches. Actual potency should always be confirmed from the laboratory label attached to the specific product.
What does Alien Mints taste like?
Vanilla, cookie dough, mint, pine, diesel, earth, and motor-oil funk define the profile. The opening can be creamy and slightly sweet, while fuel, herbs, and pepper become more noticeable through the finish.
Final Thoughts on Alien Mints
Alien Mints demonstrates that a breeder does not always need to introduce completely new genetics to create a distinctive cultivar. By backcrossing Animal Mints, Seed Junky Genetics concentrated a family already known for exceptional resin, dense flower structure, creamy sweetness, and serious potency. Alien Labs then helped establish the resulting selection as a premium cannabis cultivar, with its combination of vanilla, mint, motor oil, cookie dough, pine, and gas giving it an unmistakable identity.
The strain’s effects are equally representative of what made the Mints family influential. Cerebral elevation arrives early, but physical relaxation steadily gains ground without necessarily producing immediate couch-lock. That progression gives experienced consumers a versatile evening hybrid while still delivering the potency expected from modern exotic weed. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in the genetics behind Wedding Cake, Kush Mints, Animal Face, and the broader Seed Junky family, Alien Mints offers a concentrated look at one of the breeding lines that helped define an entire era of premium marijuana strains .

Genetics and Lineage

The breeding objective was to bring together two exceptionally resinous cultivars with complementary aromatic characteristics. WatermelonZ, also called Watermelon Zkittlez, contributes the concentrated sweetness associated with the influential Zkittlez family, while Velvet Moon introduces sour citrus, earthy depth, and structural vigor. The resulting hybrid contains approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa genetics, creating a combination that emphasizes abundant flower production without sacrificing the stimulating qualities found in its parental lines.
WatermelonZ is closely associated with Northern California’s fruit-focused cannabis breeding movement. Developed by Dying Breed Seeds, the cultivar is prized for its watermelon-candy fragrance, tropical sweetness, and substantial resin production. Its deeper ancestry is reported differently across genetic records, with Watermelon Zum Zum appearing prominently in accounts of its development. Rather than relying on an uncertain historical pedigree, the defining contribution of this parent is its distinctive fruit expression and unusually sticky trichome coverage. These characteristics helped make WatermelonZ popular among enthusiasts interested in aromatic flower and solventless cannabis concentrates .
Velvet Moon provides a more clearly documented genetic background. Created from Do-Si-Dos and Holy Punch , it combines influential American Cookies genetics with Green House Seed Co.’s established breeding lines. Do-Si-Dos traces its ancestry to Girl Scout Cookies and Face Off OG , contributing resin production, earthy sweetness, and substantial potency. Holy Punch originates from The Church and a selected Grape parent, introducing fruity aromas, strong branching, and a more cheerful psychoactive character. When combined with WatermelonZ, these genetics produce a cultivar with numerous aromatic influences and a particularly vigorous growth pattern. The breeder also describes a persistent, oily sensation on the palate, reflecting the cultivar’s particularly rich resinous character. Low-stress training and appropriate canopy management may help distribute growth more evenly and improve light penetration throughout the plant.

The breeder emphasizes the combination of flower size and exceptional resin production inherited from both parents. Amherst Super Skunk provides a contrasting foundation of sturdy growth, flower density, and substantial productivity. Its broader heritage is associated with the Skunk family , particularly the combination of Skunk #1 and Afghani influences that helped establish many powerful hybrid marijuana varieties. Together, these parent lines produce a plant with the aromatic complexity of Chemdawg and the structural strength traditionally associated with Skunk genetics.

Amnesia Kush is what happens when two very different cannabis traditions are deliberately pushed into the same plant. Dinafem paired the soaring cerebral character and commercial productivity of European Amnesia with the resin, strength, earth, and unmistakable presence of American OG Kush. The result does not behave like a simple halfway point between its parents. It grows with the enthusiasm of a sativa, forms unusually substantial flowers for that category, and begins with an energetic cerebral rush before the Kush influence gradually adds physical weight. Its aroma follows the same pattern: bright lemon and sweet citrus appear first, followed by spice, pine, and a deeper earthy note that becomes more apparent once the flower is broken apart.
The cultivar also solves several problems traditionally associated with long-flowering Haze-dominant marijuana . Rather than producing narrow, airy flowers on an uncontrollably lanky plant, Amnesia Kush develops large calyxes, sturdy branches, and substantial yields within a 60–70-day bloom. Dinafem selected it to retain Amnesia’s vitality and mental intensity while introducing enough OG Kush influence to strengthen the structure, shorten internodes, and deepen the finished smoke. For growers who enjoy energetic cannabis but want larger flowers and a more physical finish, this hybrid offers a carefully engineered meeting point between Dutch Haze culture and California Kush breeding.
Genetics and Lineage
Dinafem created Amnesia Kush by crossing Amnesia Haze with OG Kush. The Amnesia side came from genetic material closely associated with the classic Dutch Amnesia line, which the breeder traced through Afghan and Neville’s Haze ancestry. That foundation helps explain the plant’s unusual combination of Haze-like mental effects with thicker flower formation than would normally be expected from a traditional tropical sativa. Amnesia genetics became enormously influential in European cannabis cultivation because they offered strong vigor, high resin production, large yields, and an intense cerebral effect while remaining far more practical indoors than many pure Haze lines.
OG Kush supplies the American side of the pedigree. Although the deeper historical ancestry of OG Kush remains disputed, its breeding influence is unmistakable: dense resin, strong branches, penetrating earthy-pine aromas, fuel-like depth, and a heavy physical component. Dinafem used it not simply to add potency but to reshape how the Amnesia parent behaved in the garden. The resulting plants tend to be sturdier, somewhat more compact, and better able to support large flower clusters than a more conventional Haze-dominant cultivar.
The hybrid remains clearly sativa dominant despite the Kush contribution. Dinafem’s current specification places it at roughly 70% sativa and 30% indica, which matches the way the plant develops and the order in which its effects appear. Vigorous growth, rapid rooting, strong upward momentum, and an energetic opening all point toward Amnesia influence, while the increasingly relaxing finish, denser floral structure, and earthy resin character reveal OG Kush underneath. That division of traits is one reason the strain feels distinct rather than like a generic Haze-Kush cross.
Effects and Experience
The first phase can arrive quickly and with considerable mental energy. Thoughts become more animated, sensory details stand out, and routine activities may feel unusually absorbing. Conversation, music, visual media, writing, or creative work can all fit this portion of the experience because the cerebral effect tends to dominate before the body becomes noticeably heavy. Dinafem specifically characterizes the strain as initially cerebral, and that description captures the way Amnesia influence announces itself almost immediately.
Time changes the experience. The sharp mental lift begins to smooth out, and the Kush side introduces a deeper feeling through the shoulders, back, and limbs. Physical relaxation grows without completely erasing the earlier mental clarity, creating a broad middle stage in which the consumer can feel both stimulated and physically settled. Stronger servings make that transition much more pronounced and can eventually turn the experience from active and social into slower, heavier, and distinctly more introspective.
With breeder-listed THC around 15–20%, Amnesia Kush may appear modest beside some contemporary cultivars, but cannabinoid percentage alone does not describe its intensity. The fast cerebral onset can feel powerful, especially to people sensitive to energetic sativa effects. Excessive consumption may produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, racing thoughts, or temporary anxiety before the physical relaxation becomes more noticeable. Moderate dosing better preserves the strain’s defining progression from mental acceleration into body-centered calm.
Medical Benefits
The two-stage effect may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who want mental uplift without committing immediately to sedation. During the earlier portion, the brighter cerebral state may make stress, low mood, or mental fatigue feel less dominant, particularly in low-pressure situations where creativity or social engagement is still desirable. As the session progresses, physical relaxation becomes more important, which may help take attention away from muscular tightness or generalized discomfort.
Larger servings can shift the cultivar toward a much calmer evening experience. The body can feel increasingly heavy, appetite may become more noticeable, and mental activity gradually becomes less urgent. That makes dosage especially relevant: a smaller amount may feel stimulating and functional, while a stronger serving can become far more relaxing. Consumers prone to THC-related anxiety may prefer conservative doses because the early Amnesia-style cerebral rush can become uncomfortable before the Kush side has time to settle it.
Limonene is particularly associated with the strain’s aromatic chemistry and matches its prominent lemon and citrus character. Spicy, piney, herbal, and earthy notes suggest additional terpene complexity, but exact ratios depend on the individual plant and cultivation environment. Medical use is better guided by testing from the actual batch, personal cannabinoid tolerance, medications, and previous response to cannabis rather than assuming every harvest will produce identical effects.
Flavor Profile and Aroma
Fresh citrus dominates the opening aroma. Lemon zest is especially noticeable, accompanied by a sweeter fruit quality that gives the flower more depth than a sharp lemon-only strain. The profile can feel bright and almost sparkling when a mature bud is first opened, reflecting the Amnesia parent far more strongly than the earthy Kush side during that initial impression.
Breaking apart the flower reveals the heavier layers. Spice appears beneath the citrus, followed by pine, dried herbs, and earthy resin. OG Kush adds enough depth to prevent the bouquet from becoming purely fruity, while the Amnesia influence keeps the heavier notes from overwhelming the brighter top end. Properly cured flower can therefore shift repeatedly between sweet lemon, spice, evergreen, and soil depending on how it is handled.
The same sequence appears in the flavor. Citrus and sweetness tend to lead on the inhale, while pine, spice, and a darker Kush-like earthiness become stronger through the exhale. Vaporization highlights the lemon and fruit particularly well, whereas combustion gives more weight to spice and resin. Slow drying and patient curing matter because the most volatile citrus compounds can disappear quickly if harvested marijuana is exposed to excessive heat or dried too aggressively.
Growing Information
Amnesia Kush is vigorous enough that indoor growers need to control its size early rather than trying to correct excessive stretch after flowering has begun. Dinafem specifically recommends keeping the vegetative period relatively short when vertical space is limited, with about three weeks of vegetation serving as a practical ceiling in many indoor setups. Plants root quickly, develop energetic vertical growth, and can become surprisingly large if given unrestricted space. Topping, low-stress training , or a screen can help spread that vigor horizontally and keep productive flower sites evenly exposed to light.
Indoor flowering requires approximately 60–70 days, with yields around 500–600 g/m² under optimized conditions. The plant forms large, hard flower clusters built from prominent calyxes rather than the thin, loose buds associated with traditional long-flowering sativas. Dinafem also notes that the cultivar does not require unusually aggressive feeding despite its productivity. Balanced nutrition is preferable because excessive fertilization can compromise aroma and finished flower quality. Strong odor control is worthwhile indoors, as mature plants can become extremely fragrant.
Outdoor cultivation reveals the full scale of the genetics. Plants can approach 3 meters in height and produce roughly 600–800 grams each under favorable conditions, with harvest arriving around mid-October. The sativa-dominant structure handles humidity better than many dense indica plants because it does not retain moisture as readily, making the strain comparatively suitable for humid or tropical environments. Even so, good airflow and protection from prolonged late-season rain remain important once the flowers become large and resinous.
FAQ
What strains make Amnesia Kush?
Dinafem created Amnesia Kush by crossing Amnesia Haze with OG Kush. The Amnesia parent carries strong Dutch Haze influence, while OG Kush contributes American Kush structure, resin, earth, pine, and physical relaxation.

How much THC does Amnesia Kush have?
Dinafem lists the cultivar at approximately 15–20% THC with low CBD. Actual cannabinoid levels vary according to phenotype, lighting, cultivation method, harvest timing, and environmental conditions.
What does Amnesia Kush taste like?
The main flavors are lemon, citrus, sweet fruit, spice, pine, and earthy Kush. The brighter Amnesia notes generally appear first, while the darker OG character becomes stronger toward the finish.
How long does Amnesia Kush take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 60–70 days. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity around mid-October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Amnesia Kush
Amnesia Kush succeeds because neither parent is reduced to a minor background influence. Amnesia Haze controls much of the plant’s vigor, production, citrus aroma, and cerebral intensity, while OG Kush reshapes the structure and adds resin, earth, pine, and an increasingly physical finish. The result feels like a deliberate fusion of two cannabis traditions rather than a strain carrying two famous names for marketing purposes.
Its cultivation traits reinforce that balance. A 60–70-day indoor flowering period is manageable for a predominantly sativa plant, while yields of roughly 500–600 g/m² indoors and 600–800 grams per plant outdoors give the cultivar legitimate production value. Vigorous stretch requires planning, but sturdy branches, substantial flowers, and reasonable nutritional needs keep the plant from becoming unnecessarily difficult.
For consumers, the most memorable quality is the progression of the experience. Bright lemon and sweet fruit introduce a fast cerebral high, spice and pine add depth to the flavor, and the body gradually becomes calmer as the OG Kush influence develops. Amnesia Kush remains a strong example of purposeful hybrid breeding—combining Dutch Haze energy with California Kush weight in a cannabis strain that offers both substantial garden performance and a distinctly layered effect.

This is one reason Amnesia Lemon has remained popular with people who prefer marijuana that contributes energy rather than immediately slowing the day down.
As the initial cerebral wave settles, the 40% indica influence becomes easier to recognize. Outdoor Yield: Up to 100 grams per plant
