Genetics and Lineage
Resin Seeds identifies the direct cross as Yumbolt × G13 Haze and provides an important detail about the maternal side: the Yumbolt used in the project was a special plant selected in 2003. The breeder wanted to retain that plant’s sweetness and relaxing qualities while introducing additional spice and a slower-building cerebral effect from G13 Haze. This was therefore not simply a generic crossing of whatever Yumbolt and Haze plants happened to be available; the selection of the Yumbolt female was central to the project.
Yumbolt itself was created by Sagarmatha Seeds from old Humboldt County material. Sagarmatha describes the line as having roots believed to trace back to Afghan genetics that became established in Humboldt County, California, during the late 1970s. It became particularly famous for exceptionally sweet flavor, dense frosted flowers, and a comfortable, dreamy stone. Yumbolt also won first place in the Seeds Indica category at the 2001 High Times Cannabis Cup , giving the maternal side of Yummy an established competition pedigree.
G13 Haze contributes a very different genetic direction. Mr. Nice Seedbank identifies its classic G13 Haze as G13 × Haze , combining a predominantly Afghan-derived G13 side with an inbred Haze family . The parent is valued for potency, flavor, and strong hybrid-breeding potential, while its Haze ancestry introduces longer-lasting cerebral intensity and aromatic spice. Bringing that male to Yumbolt created a cultivar in which Afghan-influenced sweetness and body relaxation meet the brighter, more expansive qualities of classic Haze.
Effects and Experience

Mood softens, the body becomes less tense, and music, conversation, food, or low-pressure activities can become more enjoyable without an immediate sense of mental overload. G13 Haze changes the experience as time passes. The breeder describes the high as having a creeping quality, meaning its full strength may not be obvious immediately after consumption. Mental activity can gradually become more pronounced, with thoughts becoming more associative, sensory details more interesting, and the overall experience taking on a stronger cerebral edge. The cultivar therefore behaves differently from weed that peaks almost immediately and then steadily declines.
At 19–23% THC, potency is meaningful without being defined by extreme modern laboratory numbers. Medical Benefits
No controlled clinical research has evaluated Yummy itself as a treatment for a specific disease or symptom. Research into cannabis and cannabinoids more generally suggests modest benefit for certain forms of chronic pain and has examined cannabinoids for sleep, nausea, appetite, and several neurological conditions. A seed-grown THC-rich cannabis cultivar is not chemically standardized in the way a pharmaceutical preparation is, so findings from cannabinoid studies cannot simply be assigned to Yummy.
The strain’s THC content also creates potential disadvantages. Larger doses can impair attention, memory, judgment, and coordination, while susceptible individuals may experience anxiety or dizziness. Cannabinoids can interact with some medications as well. Medical consumers should therefore use current cannabinoid testing and appropriate professional guidance rather than assuming the strain name or its relaxing reputation predicts a specific therapeutic effect.
Flavor Profile and Aroma
Sweetness forms the backbone of Yummy’s flavor. The G13 Haze male supplies the contrast. Resin Seeds highlights spice as one of the traits added by that parent, while the broader G13/Haze family brings dry herbal, earthy, woody, citrus, and incense-like possibilities into the aromatic range. Properly cured flower can therefore move from sweet fruit on the opening inhale into a drier, spicier finish, with Haze character becoming more noticeable after the initial sweetness fades.
No authoritative Resin Seeds laboratory terpene profile has been published for Yummy. The documented breeder description is more reliable: strong Yumbolt sweetness combined with additional G13 Haze spice. Harvest conditions and curing also matter considerably. Excessive drying heat can erase brighter fruit and citrus notes, leaving a flatter mixture of wood, herbs, and earth.
Growing Information
Resin Seeds gives Yummy an indoor flowering period of 9–10 weeks. That relatively long bloom reflects its 60% sativa classification and G13 Haze ancestry but remains much more manageable than many traditional Haze plants. Growers should anticipate a plant with enough sativa influence to benefit from canopy control. Training before and during the early flowering stretch can help distribute branches across the available light footprint rather than allowing one or two shoots to dominate vertically. Maintaining airflow through the interior canopy becomes increasingly important as flowers gain weight, while removing unnecessary shaded growth can help direct plant energy toward well-lit bud sites.
Outdoor cultivation is scheduled for September through October according to Resin Seeds, with breeder-listed production of approximately 150–300 grams per plant. Climate therefore matters. Gardens with dry, mild autumn weather provide more flexibility than regions where cold rain arrives early. Plants expressing more of the G13 Haze side may require additional time, while Yumbolt-influenced individuals may mature somewhat more compactly.
Post-harvest patience is particularly worthwhile. Much of the cultivar’s identity lies in the contrast between sweet fruit and Haze spice, both of which can lose clarity if flower is dried aggressively. A controlled dry followed by a steady cure allows moisture within the buds to equalize while preserving more of the volatile aromatic compounds. Properly handled Yummy should smell layered rather than merely sweet, with fruit giving way to spice, herbs, and deeper earthy notes.
FAQ

Final Thoughts on Yummy
Yummy has a much stronger pedigree than its playful name might suggest. Resin Seeds started with a Yumbolt female selected in 2003 rather than a generic sweet cultivar, then crossed it with G13 Haze to deliberately add spice and a slow-building cerebral dimension. That choice brought together two very different branches of cannabis history: old Humboldt-associated Yumbolt genetics and the famous G13/Haze breeding family.
The Yumbolt side is particularly significant. Sagarmatha’s cultivar carried a reputation for dense flowers, pronounced sweetness, a dreamy stone, and a first-place finish at the 2001 High Times Cannabis Cup. G13 Haze contributes Afghan and Haze ancestry along with greater mental intensity and breeding vigor. Yummy distills those influences into a 60/40 sativa-leaning hybrid with 19–23% THC and a 9–10 week flowering cycle.
For growers, the cultivar offers moderate production rather than enormous headline yields: approximately 400 g/m² indoors and 150–300 g per plant outdoors according to Resin Seeds. For consumers, flavor and effect are the more compelling reasons to seek it out. Sweet fruit gives way to spice and deeper Haze character, while comfortable physical relaxation is gradually joined by a cerebral high that can continue gaining strength after the initial inhale.
That progression gives Yummy an identity very different from contemporary candy strains whose appeal often begins and ends with sweetness. Its flavor is sweet because of Yumbolt, but its structure, spice, and creeping psychoactivity are equally important. For enthusiasts interested in Resin Seeds genetics, Humboldt-influenced cultivars, or older G13 Haze crosses, Yummy remains a well-documented hybrid with a genuine breeder history behind the name.

Zamosa did not become one of the more talked-about modern California hybrids simply because its parents have recognizable names. The strain proved its appeal in direct competition. LA Family Farms entered the flower at the 2025 California Zalympix and left with first place in three of the event’s most important categories: Best Overall, Best Tasting, and Best Terps/Best Smell. That sweep is particularly revealing because it points toward the quality that defines this weed better than a THC number ever could. Zamosa is fundamentally an aroma-and-flavor variety, pairing the dense candy character of Z genetics with the sparkling orange personality of Mimosa. The result can smell less like conventional dried cannabis and more like citrus soda, tropical sweets, crushed orange peel, and fruit candy over a faint earthy-skunky base.
The visual presentation fits the aromatic intensity. Commercial examples show compact flowers mixing deep purple and forest-green tissue beneath a substantial covering of trichomes, with vivid orange pistils cutting through the surface. Yet the cultivar’s appeal goes beyond appearance. Its effect can arrive with enough cerebral lift to feel lively and social before a gentler physical calm settles underneath, giving it broader usefulness than either a highly stimulating daytime strain or a heavy evening indica. Combined with THC results commonly reaching the mid-to-upper 20% range, Zamosa offers the type of modern marijuana experience aimed squarely at experienced consumers who value terpene expression as much as raw potency.
Genetics and Lineage
The direct cross is Zkittlez, frequently styled as The Original Z, paired with Mimosa. LA Family Farms is identified as the breeder, although some brand materials abbreviate the parents as “Kittlez × Mosa.” The genetic idea is straightforward but highly complementary. Z contributes concentrated candy, tropical fruit, and sweet-skunk qualities, while Mimosa introduces a much brighter citrus axis dominated by orange, tangerine, and tropical notes. Instead of one parent simply masking the other, the selected Zamosa expression allows both flavor families to remain recognizable.
Mimosa adds considerable depth to the family tree. Symbiotic Genetics created the parent by crossing Clementine with Purple Punch . Clementine supplies the sharp citrus lineage, while Purple Punch contributes sweeter fruit, resin production, and a softer physical dimension. That combination made Mimosa one of the important orange-forward hybrids of its generation. In Zamosa, those qualities meet the heavier confectionery influence of Z, turning fresh citrus into something more exaggerated—closer to orange candy, tropical soda, or sweet fruit punch than plain orange peel.
The pairing also explains why different Zamosa batches can lean in noticeably different aromatic directions without losing their basic identity. One crop may emphasize tangy orange and fizzy citrus; another can reveal more tropical candy, watermelon, floral sweetness, or skunky earth. Phenotype, environmental conditions, harvest maturity, drying, and curing all influence how those inherited characteristics appear in finished flower. What ties authentic examples together is the same basic tension between intensely sweet Z terpenes and Mimosa’s brighter citrus-fruit side.
Effects and Experience
The early phase tends to arrive above the shoulders. Rather than immediately producing a heavy physical slowdown, the cultivar can create a brighter mood, stronger sensory engagement, and an easier conversational rhythm. Music may feel richer, food more interesting, and social interaction less effortful. That cerebral movement helps explain why commercial descriptions frequently characterize the experience as euphoric and uplifting. A moderate amount may work well for an afternoon gathering, creative session, casual gaming, walking, or simply shifting out of a dull mood without immediately wanting to settle onto a couch.
What makes the high more versatile is the way the second half develops. The initial mental brightness does not necessarily keep climbing. Instead, physical calm begins filling in underneath it, creating a more grounded state that can reduce restlessness without completely erasing mental engagement. For experienced consumers, that can make Zamosa feel balanced in the practical sense of the word: energetic enough to remain interesting, yet not so sharp that the experience becomes relentlessly stimulating.
Potency can change that balance quickly. Commercial flower has been documented around 24% to more than 27% THC, with one Klutch batch testing at 24.41% THC and only 0.07% CBD. At those levels, taking substantially more can replace the clean uplift with distraction, memory impairment, anxiety, or a heavier body feeling. Someone with limited cannabis tolerance should not interpret the sweet flavor as evidence of mild potency. Modern candy weed can be extremely strong even when the smoke seems smooth and approachable.
Medical Benefits
Cannabis flower is not chemically standardized simply because two packages carry the same strain name, and cannabinoid concentrations can change considerably from harvest to harvest. Some medical cannabis patients may nevertheless prefer an uplifting hybrid when seeking temporary relief from stress, discomfort, low appetite, or difficulty relaxing without immediately becoming sleepy.
Research involving cannabis and cannabinoids more broadly offers limited support for some therapeutic applications. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes evidence suggesting modest benefits for certain kinds of chronic pain, while studies involving people with other health conditions have sometimes found improvements in sleep quality or sleep disturbance. Those findings do not demonstrate that Zamosa specifically treats pain, insomnia, anxiety, depression, or another disorder. They also involve a variety of cannabinoid preparations rather than one high-THC flower cultivar.
Its terpene profile should be interpreted with similar caution. Limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool have all appeared prominently in tested Zamosa flower, and these compounds are subjects of ongoing biological research. However, detecting a terpene in marijuana does not prove a corresponding therapeutic effect in a person. High THC can also produce dizziness, anxiety, altered judgment, or cognitive impairment, and cannabinoids may interact with some medications. Medical users should therefore base treatment decisions on professional guidance and actual product testing rather than terpene marketing or strain reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma
If Zamosa has a defining characteristic, it is the way sweet Z terpenes collide with Mimosa’s orange character. The aroma can open with a striking carbonated quality—something reminiscent of citrus soda or fruit-flavored sparkling candy—before spreading into tropical fruit, orange zest, and dense sugar. L.A. Family Farms-associated descriptions have also noted sweet watermelon and an earthy foundation. Grinding the flower changes the balance again, often exposing a small but distinct amount of skunky funk beneath the brighter fruit.
The palate tends to unfold rather than delivering every flavor simultaneously. The first impression may be sugary and tropical, followed by tangy orange through the middle of the inhale. Citrus sharpness can persist through the exhale while floral, earthy, or lightly spicy notes remain behind. That progression is important because it keeps the cultivar from tasting like generic sweet weed. Z provides the dense candy coating, but Mimosa gives the profile enough acid and citrus brightness to keep the sweetness from becoming flat.
Analytical testing supports that sensory profile while also showing why terpene claims should remain batch-specific. A Klutch-grown sample measured 1.38% total terpenes, with limonene at 0.55%, beta-caryophyllene at 0.50%, and linalool at 0.33%. Another commercial Zamosa sample showed beta-caryophyllene at 0.60%, linalool at 0.26%, limonene at 0.23%, plus smaller quantities of humulene, bisabolol, myrcene, and nerolidol. Different order, same general aromatic family. The variation demonstrates that there is no single fixed Zamosa terpene formula.
Growing Information
Detailed breeder cultivation specifications remain one of the least documented areas of Zamosa. L.A. Family Farms has publicly established the lineage and commercial identity of the cultivar, but an official grow sheet listing exact flowering duration, stretch, indoor yield, outdoor harvest date, nutrient preferences, and environmental targets has not been released. For that reason, precise claims such as a guaranteed gram-per-square-meter yield should be treated cautiously. Third-party cultivation references often place the flowering period near eight to nine weeks, but that should be viewed as a working estimate rather than a published L.A. Family Farms specification.
The visible structure of commercial flower provides some practical clues. Zamosa is capable of forming dense, resin-covered buds with strong purple and green coloration, so airflow and humidity control become increasingly important as flowers mature. Growers working with verified plant material should monitor internodal spacing and stretch during the first part of bloom before deciding how aggressively to train the canopy. Topping or low-stress training may help distribute growth where legal, but the plant itself should dictate the technique rather than assumptions based only on the behavior of Mimosa or Z.
Aroma preservation after harvest may matter almost as much as flower production. Citrus, tropical fruit, and candy impressions rely heavily on volatile aromatic compounds that can disappear rapidly when cannabis is dried too warm, left exposed to moving air for too long, or stored under heat and light. A controlled dry followed by proper curing is therefore essential if the goal is to reproduce the intensely fragrant qualities that helped Zamosa dominate the flavor and terpene categories at Zalympix. The plant may still produce potent weed after a rushed dry, but much of what makes this particular cultivar special can be lost before it reaches the jar.
FAQ
What strain is Zamosa?
Zamosa is a hybrid bred by L.A. Family Farms from Zkittlez, also known as The Original Z, crossed with Mimosa. It is a terpene-focused modern cultivar centered on sweet candy, citrus, tropical fruit, and orange flavors.
Who bred Zamosa?
L.A. Family Farms created the cultivar. The Los Angeles breeder and cultivation company is also responsible for the award-winning commercial flower that swept three major categories at the 2025 California Zalympix.
How strong is Zamosa?
The exact potency changes by harvest. Commercial flower examples have tested around 24–28% THC, with CBD generally present only in trace quantities. That places the strain firmly in the high-potency category for most consumers.
What does Zamosa taste like?
Expect sweet Z-style candy layered with orange citrus, tropical fruit, fizzy fruit-soda character, and occasional watermelon or floral notes. Breaking apart the buds can reveal earthy and lightly skunky undertones beneath the brighter sweetness.
Did Zamosa win Zalympix?
Yes. L.A. Family Farms’ Zamosa won 1st Place for Best Overall Flower, Best Tasting, and Best Terps/Best Smell at the 2025 California Zalympix, an unusually strong sweep for a single entry.
Final Thoughts on Zamosa
Zamosa has something that many fashionable cannabis strains never acquire: a competition record strong enough to support the hype around its flavor. Winning Best Overall would have been significant on its own. Taking Best Tasting and Best Terps/Best Smell at the same 2025 Zalympix event showed that the cultivar’s sensory reputation was not built solely through branding. L.A. Family Farms found a particularly effective intersection between Zkittlez and Mimosa, retaining the dense candy character of one parent while allowing the other’s orange and tropical citrus qualities to remain bright and immediately recognizable.
That combination extends into the experience. The high can open on an uplifting, euphoric note before developing enough physical relaxation to keep it from becoming excessively sharp, while commercial THC results in the mid-to-upper 20% range give the flower considerable strength. Dense trichome coverage, purple-green coloration, bright orange pistils, and a terpene profile frequently led by limonene and beta-caryophyllene further reinforce its premium presentation.
For growers, the main limitation is not the genetics but the available documentation. L.A. Family Farms has not released the kind of detailed public cultivation sheet that would justify quoting exact yields or an official flowering day. That missing information is better acknowledged than replaced with generic numbers. What is well established is more meaningful: Zamosa is a traceable L.A. Family Farms cross of Z and Mimosa, it consistently expresses an unusually vibrant candy-citrus profile, and its award history places it among the most successful flavor-focused California marijuana strains of the mid-2020s.

Strawberry fragrances are surprisingly difficult to reproduce convincingly through cannabis genetics. Many marijuana varieties advertised as berry-flavored offer little more than generalized sweetness, but Ztrawberry takes a more distinctive approach. Developed by Green House Seed Co., this indica-dominant hybrid combines the unmistakable candy character of Runtz with the rich red-fruit aromas and exceptional environmental resilience of A.M.S.

Genetics and Lineage
Ztrawberry originates from a cross between Runtz and A.M.S., two cannabis varieties developed for very different purposes. Runtz represents the modern American movement toward exceptionally sweet, high-potency genetics, while A.M.S. belongs to an earlier generation of European breeding focused on resilience and consistent outdoor performance. Green House Seed Co. selected these parents to preserve the intense aromatic qualities of Runtz while introducing the shorter internodes, robust branching, and fungal resistance associated with A.M.S. The resulting cultivar contains approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa genetics, creating a balanced plant with substantial flower density and a psychoactive profile that evolves noticeably during consumption.
Runtz descends from Zkittlez and Gelato #33 , two influential California cannabis varieties associated with contemporary dessert-style breeding. Zkittlez contributes the colorful candy-like fragrance and concentrated tropical sweetness that helped establish an entire category of fruit-forward marijuana . Gelato #33, itself descended from Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies , introduces creamy aromas, earthy complexity, and considerable cannabinoid potency. A.M.S., meanwhile, stands for Anti Mold Strain and was developed by Green House Seed Co. from two older Swiss cannabis selections, generally identified as Swiss sativa and Swiss indica. Its genetic history centers on plants capable of withstanding difficult outdoor conditions while producing compact flowers and a distinctive fragrance reminiscent of overripe red berries and fruit preserves. Bringing these parental lines together allows Ztrawberry to express both the confectionery qualities of modern American weed and the durable architecture associated with traditional European cultivation.
Effects and Experience
The psychoactive progression of Ztrawberry is notable because its initial intensity gradually gives way to a lighter, more mentally engaging state. Green House Seed Co. describes an immediate onset influenced by the Gelato genetics within Runtz, creating a substantial sensation of intoxication shortly after consumption. This early stage may involve noticeable physical relaxation, a change in sensory perception, and an increasingly euphoric mood. Music and familiar surroundings can become more absorbing, while stressful thoughts may temporarily feel less prominent. Although the cultivar contains predominantly indica genetics, its character extends beyond the heavy physical sedation commonly associated with traditional broad-leaved marijuana varieties.
As the experience develops, the influence of A.M.S. becomes more apparent. The initial intensity can gradually transition into a brighter cerebral sensation, accompanied by a sense of mental stimulation and increased interest in conversation or recreational activities. Rather than following the conventional pattern of energetic onset followed by eventual sedation, this hybrid may begin with a more substantial physical and psychoactive impact before settling into a comparatively lively mental state. The breeder describes the effects as long-lasting and potentially suitable for consumption throughout the day, although the reported THC concentration of approximately 22.48% means the experience should not be considered mild. Larger amounts can interfere significantly with concentration, memory, judgment, and physical coordination.
Individual responses depend on tolerance, consumption method, dosage, and the chemical composition of the harvested flower. Some consumers may experience pleasant euphoria and comfortable relaxation, while others may encounter anxiety, dizziness, dry mouth, increased heart rate, or temporary confusion. The cultivar’s relatively high THC content makes cautious dosing important, especially for individuals unfamiliar with potent cannabis. A stimulating mental sensation also does not guarantee functional performance, since intoxication can remain substantial even when a person feels alert.

The combination of physical relaxation and mood-altering effects may interest medical marijuana consumers managing certain forms of persistent discomfort or stress-related symptoms. Cannabinoids interact with physiological pathways involved in sensory processing, pain perception, and emotional responses. However, these findings do not establish that every THC-rich cannabis variety produces the same therapeutic outcomes. No controlled clinical trials have demonstrated that Ztrawberry itself effectively treats chronic pain or any other medical condition.
Its evolving psychoactive character may also appeal to individuals who prefer relaxation without prolonged physical heaviness. The initial calming sensation could make it easier for some consumers to unwind, while the later cerebral effects may feel more compatible with low-pressure daytime activities. Nevertheless, high-THC marijuana can aggravate anxiety, produce uncomfortable stimulation, or interfere with sleep, particularly when consumed in excessive amounts. Regular consumption may contribute to tolerance and dependence, while potential interactions with prescription medications deserve consideration. Anyone exploring cannabis for persistent medical symptoms should consult a qualified healthcare professional rather than relying exclusively on a particular strain.
Flavor Profile and Aroma
The aromatic identity of Ztrawberry begins with a remarkably concentrated impression of ripe red fruit. Freshly handled flowers release a fragrance reminiscent of strawberries, berry preserves, and sweet fruit syrup, reflecting the distinctive contribution of A.M.S. Unlike lighter floral cannabis varieties, the berry sweetness has a pungent, almost overripe quality that becomes especially noticeable when the buds are broken apart. Runtz introduces an additional layer of sugary candy and bright acidity, creating a sharper contrast against the deeper fruit notes. As the fragrance develops, creamy and earthy undertones associated with Gelato become more prominent, producing a rounded aromatic profile that moves beyond straightforward strawberry sweetness.
Green House Seed Co. emphasizes the interaction between these parental aromas but does not provide a definitive dominant-terpene ranking for the cultivar. Myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene are plausible contributors to its broader herbal, citrus, and spicy characteristics, although their actual concentrations require strain-specific laboratory testing. Myrcene can contribute earthy and musky qualities, limonene introduces fresh citrus impressions, and caryophyllene provides peppery warmth. The recognizable strawberry fragrance may also involve additional volatile compounds beyond the major terpenes commonly listed on cannabis laboratory reports. During consumption, sweet berry and candy flavors can dominate the initial impression before transitioning toward cream, subtle citrus acidity, and an earthy finish. Proper drying, curing, and airtight storage help preserve the delicate aromatic components responsible for this layered sensory experience.
Growing Information
Ztrawberry develops a strong, bushy structure that reflects the stabilizing influence of A.M.S. while retaining several distinctive characteristics associated with Runtz. The plant produces substantial branches capable of supporting heavy flowers, accompanied by relatively short internodal distances that create a compact arrangement of developing bud sites. Its foliage generally displays a darker green coloration inherited from the Swiss-derived parent, although individual phenotypes may vary in leaf shape and color intensity. Flowering generally requires eight to nine weeks under controlled indoor conditions. This unusually compact floral structure gives the flowers substantial density and considerable visual appeal. Resin production becomes increasingly prominent as harvest approaches, covering the buds with a frosted appearance that contrasts with the darker foliage. Some plants may express purple coloration late in flowering, although this characteristic is not guaranteed. Dense flowers require careful humidity management because trapped moisture can encourage fungal problems even in cultivars with inherited disease resistance. Proper ventilation and regular inspection remain essential throughout the final flowering stages.
Outdoor cultivation highlights one of the hybrid’s most valuable inherited characteristics: the environmental resilience associated with A.M.S. The Swiss-derived parent was selected for its ability to perform under conditions where fungal pressure and moisture can challenge more sensitive cannabis varieties. Strong sunlight, adequate root space, reliable airflow, and balanced irrigation support healthy development. Its sturdy branching and abundant resin production make it appealing to growers who value both flower quality and productivity, while the relatively short flowering schedule provides flexibility across a range of suitable climates.

The cultivar inherits a genetic background associated with fungal resistance through its A.M.S. parent, originally developed for challenging outdoor conditions. Final Thoughts on Ztrawberry
Ztrawberry illustrates how contemporary cannabis breeding can benefit from revisiting older genetics rather than relying exclusively on fashionable modern hybrids. The concentrated candy sweetness and substantial potency of Runtz combine with the distinctive red-fruit fragrance, vigorous structure, and environmental resilience of A.M.S. The result is a flavorful indica-dominant cultivar with an unusual progression of effects, moving from immediate intensity toward a more cerebral and socially engaging experience.
For cultivators, sturdy branching, compact internodal spacing, abundant trichome production, and an eight-to-nine-week flowering period provide several appealing characteristics.
